triage_records.title: Human papillomavirus and cervical cancer
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper is a review that directly addresses the causal link between persistent high-risk HPV infection and cervical cancer, stating that 99.7% of cases are caused by this specific condition and explaining the biological mechanism.

triage_records.title: The Rsearch of Health Management for Prevention and Treatment of Cervical Persistent High-risk HPV Infection
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper investigates the efficacy of health management interventions for treating persistent high-risk HPV infection. It does not study the causal relationship between persistent HPV infection and the development of cervical cancer (the specific outcome in the query). The outcome measured is HPV clearance/viral load, not cancer incidence.

triage_records.title: Screening for persistent high-risk HPV infections may be a valuable screening method for young women; A retrospective cohort study
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper presents original empirical data from a retrospective cohort study directly investigating the association between persistent high-risk HPV (hrHPV) infection and the development of high-grade cervical lesions (HSIL), which are precursors to cervical cancer. It compares the prevalence of HSIL in women with persistent hrHPV against those who cleared the infection or were negative, providing direct evidence on the causal link between persistent infection and cervical pathology.

triage_records.title: The Epidemiology of Human Papillomavirus Infection and Cervical Cancer
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper is a review of the epidemiology of HPV and cervical cancer. It explicitly states that the association is causal, that HPV DNA is found in all invasive cervical cancer specimens, and that HPV infection is a necessary cause. It also discusses persistence (implied by 'HPV DNA persistency' in the context of HIV and progression) and co-factors. This directly synthesizes the evidence for the causal link between persistent high-risk HPV and cervical cancer.

triage_records.title: The presence of persistent high‐risk hpv genotypes in dysplastic cervical lesions is associated with progressive disease: Natural history up to 36 months
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper presents original empirical data from a prospective cohort study demonstrating that persistent high-risk HPV infection is associated with the progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) to CIN III (a pre-cancerous lesion). While the endpoint is CIN III rather than invasive cervical cancer, the study directly addresses the causal link between persistent high-risk HPV and the development of severe cervical dysplasia, which is the immediate precursor to cancer. It provides strong evidence for the mechanism and progression pathway queried.
